title: Three-Dimensional Domain Structure of BiFeO3 by Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Magnetoelectric coupling in multiferroic BiFeO3 (BFO) enables electric-field control of magnon transport, underscoring its potential as a promising candidate for energy-efficient spintronic devices. The coupling arises from the interplay between ferroelectric (FE) polarization and antiferromagnetic order, which are spatially modulated by three-dimensional (3D) domain structures [1,2]. These structures incorporate symmetry-breaking interfaces, where localized electric field gradients and lattice distortions mediate spin-charge coupling. However, the deterministic design of magnetoelectric responses necessitates atomic-scale insights into the 3D domain structures, which remain elusive in conventional imaging techniques due to their insufficient depth resolution.
